title: Java Next
summary: From Valhalla to Leyden, from Babylon to Panama, from Amber to Detroit - big projects are shaping Java's present and future. Let's take a closer look at how they have been and will keep improving Java.
content:
From Valhalla to Leyden, from Babylon to Panama, from Amber to Detroit - big projects are shaping Java's present and future. Let's take a closer look at how they have been and will keep improving Java.

Java's big projects are shaping its present and future. Over recent years, Amber and Leyden, Panama and Loom have greatly improved the language, APIs, and runtime. But they're not done yet! And neither are Valhalla and Babylon - in fact they're just getting started. Time to take a closer look at how...

  • Project Valhalla mends the rift in Java's type system
  • Project Leyden improves Java's startup and warmup time
  • Project Babylon extends the reach of Java to foreign programming models and hardware
  • Project Panama cuts through the isthmus separating Java from native code
  • Project Amber makes the language more expressive and ready for today's and tomorrow's problems
  • Project Loom further improves efficient, structured concurrency
  • Project Detroit allows simple interop with Python and JavaScript

After this talk, you will know what to expect from Java in the next few years.
